name: Release Please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ vars.RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

   483→            # (api service inherits env vars from env_file in compose)
   484→            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
   485→              api node dist/run-migrations.js
   486→
   487→            # Start/restart services
   488→            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d
   489→
   490→            # Restart Caddy to pick up refreshed web files bind mount
   491→            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)
   492→            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml restart caddy
   493→
   494→            # Cleanup old images
   495→            docker image prune -f
   496→
   497→  provision-dashboard:
   498→    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
   499→    needs: [deploy-vps]
   500→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   501→    environment: staging
   502→    permissions:
   503→      contents: read
   504→    steps:
   505→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   506→        with:
   507→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
   508→
   509→      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
   510→        env:
   511→          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
   512→          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
   513→          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
   514→          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
   515→        run: |
   516→          set -euo pipefail
   517→          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
   518→          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
   519→          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
   520→          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
   521→          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
   522→
   523→          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
   524→          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
   525→          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
   526→            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
   527→                 'del(.__inputs)

   531→                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs

   537→            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then

   540→          fi

   544→            dashboard: $dashboard,
   545→            overwrite: true,
   546→            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
   547→          }')

   551→            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
   552→            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
   553→            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
   554→            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

file.content:
name: Deploy Staging

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*-staging*'
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      staging_tag:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  # Resolve tag: workflow_call passes it as input, push trigger uses ref_name
  DEPLOY_TAG: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  build-api:
    name: Build & Push API Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-api" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: apps/api/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:latest

  build-tee:
    name: Build & Push TEE Worker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "TEE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-tee-worker" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: ./tee-worker
          file: tee-worker/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:latest

  build-web:
    name: Build Web App
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - name: Build web app with staging env vars
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}

      - name: Upload web dist as artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: apps/web/dist/
          retention-days: 1

  create-desktop-release:
    name: Create Desktop Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          TAG="${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}"
          BODY="Staging build for ${TAG}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch), Windows (unsigned - click \"More info\" > \"Run anyway\"), and Linux (AppImage/deb)."
          # Create the release if it doesn't exist yet; ignore error if it does
          gh release create "$TAG" \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --title "CipherBox Desktop ${TAG}" \
            --notes "$BODY" \
            --prerelease 2>/dev/null || true

  build-desktop:
    name: Build Desktop App (macOS)
    needs: [create-desktop-release]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Install FUSE-T
        run: |
          brew install --cask fuse-t
          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
          sudo ln -sf "/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'CipherBox Desktop ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch) and Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway").'
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: true

  build-desktop-windows:
    name: Build Desktop App (Windows)
    needs: [create-desktop-release]
    runs-on: windows-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Install WinFsp
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          $proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","`"$out`"","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow -PassThru
          if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode)" }
          # winfsp-sys build.rs reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp\InstallDir
          # to find headers/libs. The MSI doesn't reliably write this key on CI runners.
          $installDir = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp"
          if (!(Test-Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp")) {
            New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Force | Out-Null
          }
          New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -Value $installDir -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
          # Verify registry key was written correctly
          $regVal = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -ErrorAction Stop
          if (-not $regVal.InstallDir -or $regVal.InstallDir -ne $installDir) {
            throw "WinFsp InstallDir registry mismatch: expected '$installDir', got '$($regVal.InstallDir)'"
          }
          Write-Host "WinFsp InstallDir registry: $($regVal.InstallDir)"
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\lib")) { throw "WinFsp lib directory not found at $installDir\lib" }
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\inc")) { throw "WinFsp inc directory not found at $installDir\inc" }

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: windows-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: windows-cargo-

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'CipherBox Desktop ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch), Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway"), and Linux (AppImage/deb).'
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: true
          args: -- --no-default-features --features winfsp

  build-desktop-linux:
    name: Build Desktop App (Linux)
    needs: [create-desktop-release]
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            libxdo-dev \
            libfuse3-dev \
            pkg-config \
            build-essential

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'CipherBox Desktop ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch), Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway"), and Linux (AppImage/deb).'
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: true
          args: -- --no-default-features --features fuse

  deploy-vps:
    name: Deploy to Staging VPS
    needs: [build-api, build-tee, build-web]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Download web dist artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: web-dist/

      - name: Generate .env.staging
        run: |
          cat > .env.staging << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=staging
          CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          PORT=3000
          DB_HOST=postgres
          DB_PORT=5432
          DB_USERNAME=${{ vars.STAGING_DB_USERNAME }}
          DB_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_DB_PASSWORD }}
          DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_staging
          JWT_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_JWT_SECRET }}
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${{ vars.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS }}
          IPFS_PROVIDER=local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://ipfs:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://ipfs:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190
          REDIS_HOST=redis
          REDIS_PORT=6379
          TEE_WORKER_URL=http://tee-worker:3001
          TEE_WORKER_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET }}
          REDIS_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_URL }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_API_KEY=${{ secrets.SENDGRID_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL=${{ vars.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL }}
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          ENVEOF
          # Append image tag and lowercase owner (can't use shell vars in quoted heredoc)
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          echo "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=${OWNER,,}" >> .env.staging
          echo "TAG=${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}" >> .env.staging

      - name: Copy files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: '.env.staging,docker/docker-compose.staging.yml,docker/Caddyfile,docker/alloy-config.river'
          target: /opt/cipherbox
          strip_components: 0

      - name: Arrange files on VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            # Move files to correct locations
            mv /opt/cipherbox/.env.staging /opt/cipherbox/docker/.env.staging 2>/dev/null || true
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Docker Compose reads .env automatically for variable substitution
            cp .env.staging .env

            # Restrict env file permissions (contains secrets)
            chmod 600 .env .env.staging

            # Ensure certs symlink exists for Caddy
            rm -rf /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs
            ln -sf /opt/cipherbox/certs /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs

      - name: Deploy web app files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: 'web-dist/*'
          target: /opt/cipherbox/web
          strip_components: 1
          rm: true

      - name: Deploy services
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Login to GHCR
            echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin

            # Set image tag from git tag (GHCR requires lowercase owner)
            export TAG="${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}"
            OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
            export GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER="${OWNER,,}"

            # Pull new images
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml pull

            # Run database migrations before starting services
            # (api service inherits env vars from env_file in compose)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
              api node dist/run-migrations.js

            # Start/restart services
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d

            # Restart Caddy to pick up refreshed web files bind mount
            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml restart caddy

            # Cleanup old images
            docker image prune -f

  provision-dashboard:
    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
    needs: [deploy-vps]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"

          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
                 'del(.__inputs)
                  | .id = null
                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

          if [[ ! "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Grafana API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json

Staging has always been a manual step: you push a staging-specific tag to trigger deployment. To deploy v0.25.0 to staging:

```bash
git tag v0.25.0-staging-rc-1 v0.25.0
git push origin v0.25.0-staging-rc-1
```

This tags the same commit as `v0.25.0` with a staging tag, which will trigger the deployment workflow.

Would you like me to do that, or were you expecting a different behavior (e.g., auto-deploy to staging on every release)?

file.content:
name: Tag Staging Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: 'Release tag to deploy (e.g. v0.3.0)'
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  validate-tag:
    name: Validate Release Tag
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Validate release tag exists
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}
        run: |
          if ! git rev-parse "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::Tag '${RELEASE_TAG}' does not exist"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Tag ${RELEASE_TAG} validated"

  web-e2e:
    name: Web E2E
    needs: validate-tag
    uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}
    secrets: inherit

  desktop-e2e:
    name: Desktop E2E
    needs: validate-tag
    uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-desktop.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}
    secrets: inherit

  tag-staging:
    name: Create Staging Tag
    needs: [web-e2e, desktop-e2e]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging-approval
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      staging_tag: ${{ steps.rc.outputs.staging_tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Calculate next RC number
        id: rc
        env:
          TAG: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}
        run: |
          # Find existing staging RCs for this version
          LAST_RC=$(git tag -l "${TAG}-staging-rc-*" | sed "s/${TAG}-staging-rc-//" | sort -n | tail -1)
          if [ -z "$LAST_RC" ]; then
            NEXT_RC=1
          else
            NEXT_RC=$((LAST_RC + 1))
          fi
          STAGING_TAG="${TAG}-staging-rc-${NEXT_RC}"
          echo "staging_tag=${STAGING_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "## Staging Tag" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "Creating **${STAGING_TAG}** from ${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Create and push staging tag
        env:
          STAGING_TAG: ${{ steps.rc.outputs.staging_tag }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release_tag }}
        run: |
          git tag "${STAGING_TAG}" "${RELEASE_TAG}"
          git push origin "${STAGING_TAG}"

  deploy:
    name: Deploy Staging
    needs: tag-staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
    with:
      staging_tag: ${{ needs.tag-staging.outputs.staging_tag }}
    secrets: inherit

# CipherBox API - Multi-stage Docker build
# Build from repo root: docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile -t cipherbox-api .

# Stage 1: Install dependencies and build TypeScript
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@10 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY packages/crypto/package.json packages/crypto/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @cipherbox/api...
COPY apps/api/ apps/api/
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build

# Create standalone deployment (flat node_modules, no symlinks)
RUN pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api deploy /deploy --prod --legacy

# Stage 2: Production runtime
FROM node:22-alpine AS production
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -u 1001 -G appgroup
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=build /deploy/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/apps/api/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /deploy/package.json ./package.json

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=3000

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

content.text:
OK so `@cipherbox/api` doesn't actually import any workspace packages. The `packages/crypto/package.json` COPY in the Dockerfile is a leftover, and it's now pulling in the `@cipherbox/core` dependency chain via the lockfile.

Two options:

1. **Remove the crypto COPY** — the API doesn't use it, so it shouldn't be in the Docker build

message.content: i do find it a bit strange that the api layer does not depend on any of the core packages, but guess that the api-client is sort-of the mapping layer between the api and the rest of the system.

content.text:
Yeah, it actually makes architectural sense for CipherBox specifically — the API is a zero-knowledge server that never handles plaintext or performs encryption. It just stores/retrieves opaque blobs, manages auth, and proxies IPFS. So it genuinely has no reason to import `@cipherbox/core` (shared client-side types) or `@cipherbox/crypto`.

The `api-client` is generated from the API's OpenAPI spec (`pnpm api:generate`), so it acts as the typed bridge — the API defines the contract via its controllers/DTOs, and the generated client gives the web/desktop apps type-safe access without any shared code dependency.

Shall I go ahead and get that Dockerfile fix onto a branch and pushed?

message.content: yeah lets get that docker fix up - think it can be a chore(ci) branch and PR? do we need release please to create a 0.25.1 tag here, or will pushing to main and kicking off tag-staging-release action work out?

content.text:
The Tag Staging Release action checks out the release tag's commit, so `v0.25.0` won't have the Dockerfile fix. You'd need a `v0.25.1` tag that includes it.

The catch: `chore` commits don't trigger a release-please version bump — only `feat` and `fix` do. So with `chore(ci)`, release-please won't create a new release PR.

Given that this is genuinely fixing a broken build, `fix(ci)` is arguably more accurate and would trigger the patch bump to `v0.25.1`. Up to you — want to go with `fix(ci)` so release-please picks it up?

content.text:
Found the problem. Your `pull-request-title-pattern` is `"chore: release"` without `${component}`. With the new multi-package config, release-please can't match the merged PR #298 back to its components:

```
⚠ PR component: undefined does not match configured component: cipher-box
⚠ PR component: undefined does not match configured component: @cipherbox/core
...
⚠ There are untagged, merged release PRs outstanding - aborting
```

It sees PR #298 as "untagged" because it can't figure out which component it belongs to, even though all the tags exist.

The fix is to add `${component}` to the title pattern in `release-please-config.json`. For the immediate v0.25.1, you may also need to manually create the tag since release-please is stuck. Want me to:

1. Fix the config on this branch (add `${component}` to the title pattern)
2. Manually tag `v0.25.1` from the current main so you can unblock staging today

---
status: investigating
trigger: "IPNS publishes on staging take over 30 seconds each. Batch operations extremely slow."
created: 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z
updated: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
---

## Current Focus

hypothesis: TWO compounding issues: (1) delegated-ipfs.dev external service is inherently slow (~30s per publish), and (2) SDK batch delete serializes IPNS publishes per-item instead of batching metadata changes and publishing once per folder. The delegated routing is also used needlessly since the API already has DB-backed resolve.
test: Trace the full delete flow to count IPNS publishes per batch operation; check delegated routing publish timing
expecting: Each deleteToBin call triggers 2 IPNS publishes (folder + bin), all serialized. Delegated routing publish takes ~30s per call to delegated-ipfs.dev
next_action: Count IPNS publishes in batch delete flow and verify delegated routing config/timing

## Symptoms

expected: IPNS publishes should complete in a few seconds
actual: Each IPNS publish takes over 30 seconds on staging. Batch delete across multiple subfolders is extremely slow.
errors: No errors — publishes succeed, just very slowly
reproduction: Perform a batch delete of files across multiple subfolders on staging
started: Unknown — user suspects someguy sidecar config or SDK not batching publishes

## Eliminated

## Evidence

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: docker-compose.staging.yml — someguy sidecar config
  found: someguy v0.11.1 is running with SOMEGUY_DHT=standard but it is NOT used by the delegated routing client. The DelegatedRoutingClient defaults to 'https://delegated-ipfs.dev' (external), not someguy (http://someguy:8190). Someguy is present but the API doesn't route through it.
  implication: Every IPNS publish goes to external delegated-ipfs.dev service over the internet, which could be slow. Someguy is wasted.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: DelegatedRoutingClient (apps/api/src/ipns/delegated-routing.client.ts)
  found: Default URL is 'https://delegated-ipfs.dev'. 10s timeout per request, 3 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s). On rate-limit (429), also retries. A single publish attempt can take up to 10s (timeout), and with retries up to ~37s worst case.
  implication: If delegated-ipfs.dev is slow or rate-limited, each publish takes 10-30s. This is the likely source of the 30s per publish.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: IpnsService.publishRecord (apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts)
  found: The DB upsert happens BEFORE the delegated routing publish. The delegated routing publish is awaited and its error is caught (non-fatal). The API batch endpoint (publishBatch) processes 10 records concurrently via Promise.allSettled. However, the SDK-level batch delete doesn't use this batch endpoint.
  implication: The API already has a batch publish endpoint, but the SDK delete flow calls individual publishes sequentially.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: SDK batch delete flow (useFolderMutations.ts handleDeleteItems -> client.deleteToBin -> bin addToBin)
  found: handleDeleteItems loops over items calling client.deleteToBin() SEQUENTIALLY. Each deleteToBin call: (1) calls updateFolderMetadataAndPublish (encrypt, IPFS add, IPNS publish = 1 delegated routing call), then (2) calls saveBinMetadata which calls createAndPublishIpnsRecord (another IPNS publish = 1 more delegated routing call). So deleting N items = 2N sequential IPNS publishes to delegated-ipfs.dev.
  implication: Deleting 5 items across subfolders = 10 sequential IPNS publishes, each taking ~30s = ~300 seconds total. This is the root cause of the batch slowness.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: Delegated routing publish vs someguy
  found: The API has DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env var config, defaulting to 'https://delegated-ipfs.dev'. The someguy container listens on port 8190. If DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL were set to 'http://someguy:8190', publishes would go through the local sidecar instead of the external service.
  implication: Routing through local someguy would be dramatically faster than going to delegated-ipfs.dev for each publish. This is the primary fix for the 30s per-publish latency.

## Resolution

root_cause: TWO compounding issues causing slow IPNS publishes:
  1. DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL defaults to external 'https://delegated-ipfs.dev' instead of the local someguy sidecar ('http://someguy:8190'). Each publish round-trips to an external service taking ~30s.
  2. SDK batch delete serializes IPNS publishes: each deleteToBin() call triggers 2 sequential IPNS publishes (folder metadata + bin metadata). N items = 2N sequential 30s publishes.

status: fixing
trigger: "Token refresh is not working on the web app. After extended use, API requests return 401 and no automatic token refresh occurs."
created: 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z
updated: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
---

## Current Focus

hypothesis: CONFIRMED - The orval-generated API functions (used for ALL app operations) go through `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts` which uses raw `fetch()` with ZERO 401 handling / token refresh logic. The token refresh interceptor exists ONLY on the hand-written axios `apiClient` in `apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts`, which is only used by the manual `authApi`, `vaultApi`, and `ipfsApi` wrappers (login/vault init paths). Once the user is logged in, almost all operations use the orval-generated functions that bypass the refresh interceptor entirely.
test: Trace which API client path each operation uses
expecting: Confirm orval-generated code lacks 401 refresh
next_action: Implement 401 token refresh logic in `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts`

## Symptoms

expected: When the access token expires, the client should automatically refresh it and retry failed requests seamlessly
actual: After the access token expires, API requests return 401 and no token refresh occurs. The user is stuck with a broken session.
errors: 401 responses from the API with no automatic recovery
reproduction: Use the staging app for an extended period, especially during long-running operations like batch deletes. Eventually the access token expires and all subsequent requests fail with 401.
started: Suspected broken for a while, exposed by slow IPNS publish (30s+) during batch operations making sessions last long enough to hit token expiry.

## Eliminated

## Evidence

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:30Z
  checked: apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts (orval mutator)
  found: Uses raw `fetch()` with no 401 detection, no retry, no token refresh. Just reads accessToken from Zustand and throws on !response.ok.
  implication: ALL orval-generated API functions (vault, ipfs, ipns, shares, invites, device-approval, etc.) have zero token refresh capability.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:35Z
  checked: apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts (hand-written axios client)
  found: Has a proper 401 response interceptor with shared refresh promise deduplication. Posts to /auth/refresh, updates Zustand store, retries original request. Also has tests in __tests__/client-refresh.test.ts.
  implication: Token refresh logic EXISTS and is correct, but it's only wired up to the hand-written apiClient used by authApi, vaultApi, and ipfsApi wrappers.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:40Z
  checked: orval.config.ts
  found: Orval is configured with `mutator: { path: './src/api/custom-instance.ts', name: 'customInstance' }` - the fetch-based instance without refresh logic.
  implication: Generated code is intentionally wired to the fetch instance, not the axios client with interceptors.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:45Z
  checked: apps/web/src/lib/api/ipfs.ts (hand-written)
  found: Also uses raw axios/fetch directly (not apiClient), reads accessToken from Zustand once, no 401 handling.
  implication: Even the hand-written IPFS functions (addToIpfs, unpinFromIpfs, fetchFromIpfs) lack token refresh — they use bare axios.post/fetch, not the interceptor-equipped apiClient.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:50Z
  checked: API token expiry
  found: Access token expires in 15 minutes (token.service.ts line 42: `expiresIn: '15m'`). Refresh token cookie set with path: '/auth', expires 7 days.
  implication: Any session lasting >15 minutes will start getting 401s from the orval-generated API calls.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:00:55Z
  checked: Which client path each operation uses
  found: Two parallel API client systems exist:
    1. `lib/api/client.ts` (axios + interceptors) -> used by authApi, vaultApi only (login + vault init paths)
    2. `api/custom-instance.ts` (raw fetch) -> used by ALL orval-generated functions (vault CRUD, IPFS, IPNS, shares, invites, device-approval, quota, etc.)
    3. `lib/api/ipfs.ts` (bare axios/fetch) -> used by upload, download, unpin services
  implication: Only the login/vault-init code path has token refresh. All runtime operations are unprotected.

## Resolution

root_cause: The web app has two separate API client systems. The orval-generated API functions (used for ALL runtime operations after login) go through `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts` which is a raw `fetch()` wrapper with no 401 handling or token refresh. The token refresh interceptor (with proper race-condition handling and shared promise deduplication) exists only in `apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts`, an axios instance used exclusively by the hand-written `authApi` and `vaultApi` wrappers during login/vault initialization. Additionally, the hand-written IPFS functions in `lib/api/ipfs.ts` also bypass the interceptor by using bare axios/fetch. Since access tokens expire in 15 minutes, any session lasting longer hits 401s with no recovery.
fix: Add 401 detection + token refresh + request retry logic to `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts`. Share the same refresh promise deduplication pattern used in `lib/api/client.ts`. Also fix `lib/api/ipfs.ts` to either use the apiClient with interceptors or add refresh logic.

DHT publish via someguy takes ~30s per record (inherent to DHT propagation). This blocks the API response for 30s. Combined with SDK serializing per-item deletes (each with 2 IPNS publishes), batch operations are O(2N * 30s).

## Symptoms

expected: IPNS publishes should complete in a few seconds
actual: Each IPNS publish takes over 30 seconds on staging. Batch delete across multiple subfolders is extremely slow.
errors: No errors — publishes succeed, just very slowly
reproduction: Perform a batch delete of files across multiple subfolders on staging
started: Unknown — user suspects someguy sidecar config or SDK not batching publishes

- hypothesis: DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL not configured for staging, still hitting external delegated-ipfs.dev
  evidence: deploy-staging.yml line 397 shows DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 - it IS configured correctly to use local someguy sidecar

## Evidence

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: docker-compose.staging.yml — someguy sidecar config
  found: someguy v0.11.1 is running with SOMEGUY_DHT=standard. deploy-staging.yml sets DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190.
  implication: Someguy IS being used. The slowness is inherent to DHT publishing (someguy still needs to propagate records to the DHT network).

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: DelegatedRoutingClient (apps/api/src/ipns/delegated-routing.client.ts)
  found: 10s timeout per request, 3 retries with exponential backoff. Even via local someguy, the actual DHT PUT operation is slow because someguy needs to find DHT peers and propagate.
  implication: DHT propagation is inherently slow (~10-30s). This cannot be sped up, only made non-blocking.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:02:00Z
  checked: IpnsService.publishRecord() line 79
  found: `await this.delegatedRouting.publish(dto.ipnsName, recordBytes)` — the delegated routing publish is AWAITED despite being labeled "best-effort" in the comment. The DB upsert at line 65 already happened. The resolve endpoint (resolveRecord) checks DB and uses it when it has newer sequence numbers. The error is already caught (non-fatal). There is NO reason to await this.
  implication: This is THE primary bottleneck. Making this fire-and-forget will make each publish return in <100ms (DB upsert time) instead of 30s.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:02:00Z
  checked: SDK batch delete flow
  found: handleDeleteItems (useFolderMutations.ts line 403) loops sequentially calling client.deleteToBin(). Each deleteToBin calls: (1) updateFolderMetadataAndPublish -> createAndPublishIpnsRecord -> API publish endpoint (30s awaited), then (2) saveBinMetadata -> createAndPublishIpnsRecord -> API publish endpoint (another 30s awaited). N items = 2N * 30s sequential.
  implication: Even after making delegated routing fire-and-forget, the serialized delete pattern remains suboptimal. But the fix for issue 1 reduces each publish from 30s to <100ms, making the serialization acceptable for now.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:02:00Z
  checked: Resolve endpoint behavior
  found: resolveRecord() (line 286) always checks DB cache and prefers it when DB sequence > network sequence. On delegated routing failure, falls back to DB. The DB is the reliable source of truth.
  implication: Making delegated routing publish fire-and-forget is safe because resolves always use DB when it's ahead of the network. The DHT publish is only needed for external IPNS resolution and TEE republishing health checks.

## Resolution

root_cause: IpnsService.publishRecord() (line 79) awaits the delegated routing DHT publish (`await this.delegatedRouting.publish(...)`) even though (a) the DB record is already saved, (b) the comment says "best-effort", (c) the error is already caught, and (d) the resolve endpoint always checks DB and prefers newer sequences. DHT propagation via someguy inherently takes ~10-30s because someguy must propagate to the wider IPFS DHT. This means every IPNS publish blocks the API response for 30s. For batch operations (e.g., deleting N items), this causes 2N * 30s = minutes of serialized waiting.

fix: Make the delegated routing publish fire-and-forget by removing the `await` and handling it as a detached promise. The DB upsert (which is the reliable source for resolves) already happens before the DHT publish. Metrics collection still works via the finally block on the detached promise.

  evidence: deploy-staging.yml line 397 shows DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190 - it IS configured correctly to use local someguy sidecar

## Evidence

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:01:00Z
  checked: docker-compose.staging.yml — someguy sidecar config
  found: someguy v0.11.1 is running with SOMEGUY_DHT=standard. deploy-staging.yml sets DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190.

  found: 10s timeout per request, 3 retries with exponential backoff. Even via local someguy, the actual DHT PUT operation is slow because someguy needs to find DHT peers and propagate.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:02:00Z
  checked: IpnsService.publishRecord() line 79
  found: `await this.delegatedRouting.publish(dto.ipnsName, recordBytes)` — the delegated routing publish is AWAITED despite being labeled "best-effort" in the comment. The DB upsert at line 65 already happened. The resolve endpoint (resolveRecord) checks DB and uses it when it has newer sequence numbers. The error is already caught (non-fatal). There is NO reason to await this.
  implication: This is THE primary bottleneck. Making this fire-and-forget will make each publish return in <100ms (DB upsert time) instead of 30s.

- timestamp: 2026-03-21T00:02:00Z
  checked: SDK batch delete flow
  found: handleDeleteItems (useFolderMutations.ts line 403) loops sequentially calling client.deleteToBin(). content.text:
Now I see the full picture. Here's what's going on:

**There are two separate orval code generations from the same OpenAPI spec:**

1. **`packages/api-client`** — generates with `client: 'axios-functions'`, using `packages/api-client/src/instance.ts` as the mutator. This is the shared, framework-agnostic package. It uses axios and has a `getAccessToken` callback injected via `setApiClientConfig()`. No 401 refresh logic — by design it delegates that to the consumer.

2. **`apps/web/src/api/`** — generates with `client: 'react-query'`, using `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts` as the mutator. This generates React Query hooks (`useQuery`/`useMutation` wrappers) directly in the web app, backed by a raw `fetch()` instance that reads tokens from Zustand.

So the web app doesn't actually use `@cipherbox/api-client` for its API calls at all — it has its own orval generation that produces React Query hooks. The `@cipherbox/api-client` package exists for non-React consumers (the SDK, desktop app, etc.).

The **only import** of `@cipherbox/api-client` in the web app is `setApiClientConfig` in `useAuth.ts`, which is presumably configuring it for SDK usage within the web app.

The duplication is intentional (different orval client modes for different consumers), but the token refresh gap was that `custom-instance.ts` (the web app's fetch mutator) had no 401 handling. The debugger's fix added it there. The separate `lib/api/client.ts` axios instance is a *third* client that predates the orval setup — used for login/vault init and the hand-written IPFS functions.

So there are effectively **three** HTTP client paths in the web app:
1. `apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts` (fetch) — orval React Query hooks
2. `apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts` (axios) — login, vault init
3. `apps/web/src/lib/api/ipfs.ts` (was bare axios/fetch) — IPFS upload/download

The debugger's fix unified the refresh logic across all three via the shared `token-refresh.ts` module. Does this answer your question, or do you want to explore consolidating these into fewer client paths?

content.text:
Honestly, not much. Looking at the actual usage:

**Almost nobody uses the react-query hooks.** The app imports the raw generated functions, not the `useXxx` hooks:

- `services/ipns.service.ts` — imports raw functions like `ipnsControllerPublish`
- `services/share.service.ts` — imports raw functions
- `services/device-approval.service.ts` — imports raw functions
- `hooks/useAuth.ts` — imports `vaultControllerGetConfig` directly
- `components/vault/VaultExport.tsx` — imports `vaultControllerExportVault` directly

The only actual react-query hook usage is `useHealthControllerCheck` in 2 places (Login page and StatusIndicator).

So you have **8,812 lines** of generated react-query wrapper code, and the app uses the hooks from maybe 1 endpoint. Everything else just calls the raw functions — which are identical to what `@cipherbox/api-client` already generates.

If you switched to importing from `@cipherbox/api-client` + a one-off `useQuery` wrapper for the health check, you'd:
- Eliminate the web orval config and all of `apps/web/src/api/` (generated code)
- Eliminate `custom-instance.ts` (the fetch mutator)
- Get token refresh for free via `setApiClientConfig({ getAccessToken })` — one place
- Kill the `lib/api/client.ts` axios instance (third client path)
- Have a single HTTP layer with auth handled in one spot

The only real work would be updating the ~15 import paths from `../api/foo/foo` to `@cipherbox/api-client`. Want me to scope this out as a refactor?

OK here's the full picture. This is a substantial but mechanical refactor. Let me scope the key decisions:

**Two things need changing in `@cipherbox/api-client`:**
1. `withCredentials: true` on the axios instance — needed for HTTP-only refresh token cookies
2. A 401 response interceptor with a `refreshAccessToken` callback — so token refresh is handled in one place

**Then in the web app:**
- Delete `apps/web/orval.config.ts` and all of `apps/web/src/api/`
- Replace all imports with `@cipherbox/api-client`
- Replace `lib/api/auth.ts`, `lib/api/vault.ts` with thin wrappers or direct imports
- Keep `lib/api/ipfs.ts` as a thin wrapper (for upload progress + download-as-Uint8Array)
- Remove `lib/api/client.ts` (the third axios client)
- One `useHealthCheck` thin react-query wrapper for the 1 endpoint that uses it

This touches ~20 files but is mostly find-and-replace. Let me delegate the implementation.

1→# CipherBox - Claude AI Rules
     2→
     3→## Project Context
     4→
     5→CipherBox is a **technology demonstrator** for privacy-first encrypted cloud storage using IPFS/IPNS and Web3Auth. It is not a commercial product.
     6→
     7→## Documentation Structure
     8→
     9→| Document                                                     | Purpose                                    |
    10→| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
    11→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/PRD.md`                    | Product requirements, user journeys, scope |
    12→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` | Encryption, key hierarchy, system design   |
    13→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/API_SPECIFICATION.md`      | Backend endpoints, database schema         |
    14→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/DATA_FLOWS.md`             | Sequence diagrams, test vectors            |
    15→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/CLIENT_SPECIFICATION.md`   | Web UI, desktop app specs                  |
    16→| `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` | Week-by-week development plan              |
    17→
    18→## Finalized Specifications
    19→
    20→**Current Version:** 1.11.1
    21→**Status:** Finalized (2026-01-20)
    22→
    23→### ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Do Not Edit Preliminary/Documentation Files
    24→
    25→All files in `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/` are **FINALIZED** specifications (version 1.10.0, status: Finalized). These documents represent the agreed-upon design and should **NOT** be modified.
    26→**If you need to make changes:**
    27→
    28→- New implementation documentation should be created in a separate location
    29→- Working notes and updates belong in `.planning/` or project-specific directories
    30→- Do not modify version numbers or content in `00-Preliminary-R&D/Documentation/` unless explicityly authorized.
    31→
    32→## Terminology Standards
    33→
    34→Always use consistent terminology:
    35→
    36→| Correct                   | Avoid                                              |
    37→| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
    38→| `publicKey`               | `pubkey`, `user_pubkey`, `ownerPublicKey`          |
    39→| `privateKey`              | `privkey`, `user_private_key`                      |
    40→| `rootFolderKey`           | `rootKey`, `root_folder_key`                       |
    41→| `ipnsName`                | IPNS entry (for identifier)                        |
    42→| `ipnsRecord`              | IPNS entry (for data structure)                    |
    43→| `folderKey`               | `subfolderKey` (unless specifically for subfolder) |
    44→| `fileKey`                 | `file_key`                                         |
    45→| `keyEpoch`                | `epoch`, `key_epoch`                               |
    46→| `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` | `encrypted_ipns_key`, `ipns_key_encrypted`         |
    47→| `teePublicKey`            | `tee_pubkey`, `TEE_public_key`                     |
    48→
    49→## Critical Security Rules
    50→
    51→1. **Never** suggest storing `privateKey` in localStorage/sessionStorage
    52→2. **Never** suggest logging sensitive keys
    53→3. **Never** suggest sending unencrypted keys to server
    54→4. **Always** use ECIES for key wrapping
    55→5. **Always** use AES-256-GCM for content encryption
    56→6. The server NEVER has access to plaintext or unencrypted keys
    57→7. **Always** encrypt `ipnsPrivateKey` with TEE public key before sending for republishing
    58→8. TEE decrypts IPNS keys in hardware only, signs, and immediately discards
    59→
    60→## API Development Workflow
    61→
    62→When working on `apps/api` code:
    63→
    64→1. **After modifying API endpoints, DTOs, or controllers**, regenerate the API client to keep the web app in sync:
    65→
    66→   ```bash
    67→   pnpm api:generate
    68→   ```
    69→
    70→   This command generates the OpenAPI spec from the API, creates the typed client for the web app, and runs lint fixes.
    71→
    72→2. **Always run `pnpm api:generate` before completing a feature** that touches the API to ensure type safety across the monorepo.
    73→
    74→3. **Commit the regenerated client files** (`apps/web/src/api/`) along with your API changes.
    75→
    76→## Code Generation Guidelines
    77→
    78→When generating code for CipherBox:
    79→
    80→1. Use TypeScript for all JavaScript code
    81→2. Use `Uint8Array` for binary data, not strings
    82→3. Use Web Crypto API for browser encryption
    83→4. Use camelCase for API fields, snake_case for database columns
    84→5. Include proper error handling for crypto operations
    85→6. Clear sensitive data from memory after use
    86→
    87→## Architecture Decisions
    88→
    89→- **Auth:** Web3Auth for key derivation, CipherBox backend for tokens
    90→- **Storage:** IPFS via Kubo for files, IPNS for metadata (all relayed via CipherBox API)
    91→- **Encryption:** Client-side only, server is zero-knowledge
    92→- **Sync:** IPNS polling (30s interval), no push infrastructure
    93→- **Desktop:** FUSE mount for transparent file access
    94→- **TEE Republishing:** Phala Cloud (primary) / AWS Nitro (fallback) for automatic IPNS republishing every 3 hours
    95→- **Key Epochs:** TEE public keys rotate with 4-week grace period for seamless migration
    96→
    97→## Out of Scope (v1.0)
    98→
    99→Do not implement or suggest implementations for:
   100→
   101→- Billing/payments
   102→- File versioning
   103→- File/folder sharing
   104→- Mobile apps
   105→- Search/indexing
   106→- Collaborative editing
   107→- Team accounts
   108→
   109→## Verification with MCP Tools
   110→
   111→### Playwright MCP Verification (REQUIRED)
   112→
   113→**ALWAYS attempt to verify application changes using Playwright MCP** when it is available. This ensures implemented features work correctly at runtime.
   114→
   115→**When to use Playwright MCP:**
   116→
   117→- After implementing UI components
   118→- After modifying styles or layouts
   119→- After adding new pages or routes
   120→- After any user-facing changes
   121→- During GSD verification phase
   122→
   123→**Verification workflow:**
   124→
   125→```typescript
   126→// 1. Navigate to the app
   127→await mcp__playwright__navigate({ url: 'http://localhost:5173' });
   128→
   129→// 2. Wait for page to load
   130→await mcp__playwright__wait({ selector: '[data-testid="app-loaded"]' });
   131→
   132→// 3. Capture screenshot for visual verification
   133→await mcp__playwright__screenshot({ fullPage: true, name: 'verification' });
   134→
   135→// 4. Verify element existence
   136→const exists = await mcp__playwright__evaluate({
   137→  script: `!!document.querySelector('.expected-element')`,
   138→});
   139→
   140→// 5. Verify computed styles (for UI work)
   141→const styles = await mcp__playwright__evaluate({
   142→  script: `
   143→    const el = document.querySelector('.target');
   144→    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
   145→    return { backgroundColor: s.backgroundColor, color: s.color };
   146→  `,
   147→});
   148→
   149→// 6. Test interactions
   150→await mcp__playwright__click({ selector: 'button.action' });
   151→await mcp__playwright__wait({ selector: '.result-element' });
   152→```
   153→
   154→**If Playwright MCP is not available:**
   155→
   156→- Document what needs human verification
   157→- Provide manual test steps
   158→- Flag items in VERIFICATION.md
   159→
   160→### Pencil MCP for Design Work
   161→
   162→**When working on UI phases**, use Pencil MCP (if available) or parse `.pen` files directly to extract design specifications as the source of truth.
   163→
   164→**Design files location:** `designs/*.pen`
   165→
   166→**Verification against design:**
   167→
   168→1. Extract design specs from Pencil file
   169→2. Verify CSS values match exactly (hex codes, pixel values)
   170→3. Use Playwright MCP to verify computed styles at runtime
   171→4. Document any discrepancies with file/line references
   172→
   173→**Reference:** See `.claude/get-shit-done/references/pencil-design-workflow.md`
   174→
   175→## Git Workflow
   176→
   177→**Branch Protection Rules:**
   178→
   179→- **NEVER push directly to `main` branch** - all changes must go through feature branches and PRs
   180→- Create feature branches with descriptive names (e.g., `feat/add-auth`, `fix/ipns-publish`)
   181→- All commits should be made on feature branches first
   182→- Merge to main only via pull requests
   183→
   184→**Branch Naming:**
   185→
   186→- `feat/` - New features
   187→- `fix/` - Bug fixes
   188→- `docs/` - Documentation updates
   189→- `refactor/` - Code refactoring
   190→- `chore/` - Maintenance tasks
   191→
   192→**Commit Messages:**
   193→
   194→Commits must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format. This is enforced by commitlint via a husky `commit-msg` hook.
   195→
   196→```text
   197→type(optional-scope): description
   198→
   199→[optional body]
   200→```
   201→
   202→Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Any scope string is allowed (e.g., `feat(api): add health endpoint`).
   203→
   204→**Releases & Versioning:**
   205→
   206→- All packages share a single unified version (currently tracked in `.release-please-manifest.json`)
   207→- [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) automates changelog generation, version bumping, and GitHub Releases
   208→- On push to `main`, the `release-please.yml` workflow creates/updates a release PR with accumulated changes
   209→- When that PR is merged, Release Please creates a GitHub Release and `vX.Y.Z` tag
   210→- Version bumps propagate to all `package.json` files, `Cargo.toml`, and `tauri.conf.json` via `release-please-config.json`
   211→- Staging deploys are triggered by pushing a tag matching `v*-staging*`. Legacy tags (e.g., `v0.1.0-staging.1`) also match but the **recommended convention** for new tags is `v<version>-staging-rc-<N>` (e.g., `v0.1.2-staging-rc-1`, `v0.1.2-staging-rc-2`). The `rc-N` suffix is a sequential counter allowing multiple staging deploys per version.
